2. This petition under Article 226 of Constitution of India has been filed seeking following reliefs:-
(i) Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to issue a writ in the nature of mandamus call for the entire record pertaining to the selection and appointment of the petitioner in Middle School Teacher Eligibility Test-2018 including the entire records of petitioner for kind perusal of this Hon'ble Court.

(ii) This Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to issue a writ in the nature of certiorari to quash impugned letter dt. 25.7.2023 (Annexure P/6(A)) issued by the respondent no.3, directing the respondent authorities concerned to initiate further proceedings for giving him joining in the allocated place of his posting i.e. at Govt.
Higher Secondary School Khurmundi, District Balaghat on the post of Middle School Teacher (English) by virtue of Appointment List (Annexure P/2) wherein his name finds place at Serial no.47 subject to final outcome of criminal case relating to FIR dt.24.6.2018 vide Crime no.439/2018 contained in Annexure P/3, in the interest of Sanjay Kumar Sonekar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94198546/
2 justice.
(iii) Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to grant any other relief which this Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case along with costs of petition."

sentences.text: It appears that petitioner was selected on the post of Middle School Teacher (English), however he is already facing criminal trial and he is on bail.

4. Without adverting to the fact as to whether pendency of criminal trial against petitioner for offence under Sections 420, 406, 409 of IPC would have invited the rejection of his candidature or not, this Court is of the considered opinion that if respondents have decided not to grant posting order to petitioner till pendency of criminal case, then it cannot be said that there is any legal impediment in the same.
Furthermore, it appears that allegations against petitioner are of embezzlement.
5. Under these circumstances where petitioner is facing criminal trial, this Court is of the considered opinion that no case is made out warranting interference.
6. Petition fails and is hereby dismissed.

(G.S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE Shubhankar Sanjay Kumar Sonekar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94198546/
